title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck studies 'linearized' versions of the loop equation (équation des lacets) that defines elements (λ,f) of a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the profinite modular group. He reduces modulo the congruence/abelian level, i.e. passes to 2x2 matrices over the profinite integers Ẑ (the 'adelic context'). The previous page states the general equation (*) [α0,ρ] = ε·E0(μ−1)·[f,σ] in GL(2,A). Here ρ is a fixed element of order 3 (or 6), σ = σ_∞ is a fixed element of order 4 (or 2 in PSL), and E0(λ) = ε0^λ with ε0 = (1 −1; 0 1) is a one-parameter unipotent subgroup. α0 and f are the unknowns, and μ ∈ A* plays the role of the cyclotomic parameter λ.

This page first remarks, without proof, that the scheme of solutions of (*) (with f, α0, μ variable) should be a smooth relative scheme of relative dimension 4. He declines to develop this general theory and treats only the adelic case A = Ẑ.

Proposition. Take α0 = (a b; c d) with det α0 = ε3 ∈ {±1}, and f = (r s; t u) ∈ SL2(Ẑ). Suppose α0 ρ α0^{-1} ρ^{-1} = ε2 ℓ0^γ [f,σ_∞] for some ε2 = ±1 and γ ∈ Ẑ. For the bottom rows (c,d) and (t,u) to occur in such a solution, it is necessary and sufficient that (85) holds: c² + cd + d² = ±(t² + u²) ∈ Ẑ*.

Why the bottom rows decide everything:
- For σ = (0 1; −1 0) and f ∈ SL2 one has σ f^{-1} σ^{-1} = ᵗf. Hence [f,σ] = f·ᵗf, which is symmetric with bottom-right entry t² + u². The next page computes exactly this: R = r² + s², S = T = rt + su, U = t² + u².
- Similarly, the bottom-right entry of [α0,ρ] is, up to the sign det α0, the Eisenstein norm form c² + cd + d².
- Left multiplication by the upper unipotent ℓ0^γ does not change the bottom row.
- So comparing bottom rows gives (86): 1/μ = ε2(t² + u²) = ε3(c² + cd + d²), with μ = 2γ + 1. This fixes ε3 and μ once ε2 is chosen. The other choice is the global sign change (ε2, ε3, μ) → (−ε2, −ε3, −μ).

The congruences (87) are then forced:
- t² + u² ∈ Ẑ* means it is odd, so t² + u² ≡ 1 mod 4, giving ε2 ≡ μ (mod 4).
- c² + cd + d² ≡ (c − d)² mod 3 and is a 3-adic unit, so it is ≡ 1 mod 3, giving ε3 ≡ μ (mod 3).
- γ = (μ − 1)/2 makes sense because μ is odd.

The next page completes the parametrization. Choose r, s with ru − st = 1; this is possible because (t,u) is locally primitive at every p. The pair (r,s) is unique up to adding λ(t,u). One then reconstructs the remaining entries A, B, C, D from R, S, T, U. Sufficiency on the α0 side similarly uses the fact that (c,d) is locally primitive, so it completes to a matrix of determinant ±1.

Number-theoretically, the solvability of the linearized loop equation is equivalent to the adelic unit μ^{-1} being represented, up to sign, simultaneously by the norm forms of Z[i] and Z[ζ3]. Both forms represent all units at p ≠ 2, 3. At 2 the form t² + u² represents only units ≡ 1 mod 4; at 3 the form c² + cd + d² represents only units ≡ 1 mod 3; the signs ε2, ε3 absorb this. So every μ ∈ Ẑ* occurs, consistent with the cyclotomic character / GT → Ẑ* being surjective.
errors: In (86) the right-hand side is written ε3(c²+cd+u²); it should be ε3(c²+cd+d²), as in (85) and as corrected on the next page (88).
The sign ambiguity is written as (−ε2,−ε3,−γ) (or −ν). With μ = 2γ+1, the map μ ↦ −μ sends γ to −γ−1, not −γ. The ambiguity is cleanly stated as (ε2,ε3,μ) ↦ (−ε2,−ε3,−μ).
The triple is said to lie in {±1}×{±1}×Ẑ*. But γ = (μ−1)/2 lies in Ẑ and is not in general a unit; it is μ that lies in Ẑ*.
The equation is written α0ρ(α0)^{-1} = ε2ℓ0^γ(fσ_∞f)^{-1}. Read literally it is garbled; from the previous page and the f·ᵗf computation it should be the commutator equation [α0,ρ] = ε2ℓ0^γ[f,σ_∞].
The claim that the solution scheme of (*) is relatively smooth of dimension 4 is asserted without proof ('qui etc.').

ideas.what: Linearization of the GT/loop equation to 2x2 matrices over Ẑ: commutator equations [α0,ρ] = ε·u^{μ−1}·[f,σ] with ρ of order 3, σ of order 4 and u unipotent.
ideas.modern_name: Image of Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type relations in SL2(Ẑ) / GL2(Ẑ) (congruence quotient of the profinite modular group)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara for GT; the image in SL2(Ẑ) is folklore (Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura)
ideas.where_published: Only the general program (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); the explicit computations are in La Longue Marche (1981, unpublished manuscript)

ideas.what: Solvability criterion: the bottom rows (c,d) of α0 and (t,u) of f must satisfy c²+cd+d² = ±(t²+u²) ∈ Ẑ*, i.e. the Eisenstein and Gaussian norm forms represent the same adelic unit 1/μ.
ideas.modern_name: Simultaneous representation by the norm forms of Z[ζ3] and Z[i] (the stabilizers of the elliptic points of orders 3 and 2)

ideas.what: Congruences ε2 ≡ μ (mod 4), ε3 ≡ μ (mod 3), with γ = (μ−1)/2, linking the signs to the cyclotomic-type parameter μ.
ideas.modern_name: Local constraints at 2 and 3 coming from the elliptic points of the modular curve

ideas.what: Assertion that the scheme of solutions (f, α0, μ) of the general equation (*) over arbitrary rings is a smooth relative scheme of relative dimension 4.
ideas.modern_name: Smoothness of a representation-type variety of commutator equations in GL2

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes studying the commutator equation [α0,ρ] = ε·E0(μ−1)·[f,σ] over arbitrary rings A as a scheme, asserts it is smooth of relative dimension 4, and says the whole § should generalize with 'substantial complements'. He then restricts to the adelic case.
missed.quote: voire d'interprétations schématiques des genres que le schéma des solutions de (*) (pour f, α0, μ variables) est un schéma relatif lisse de dimension relative 4, qui etc.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A scheme-theoretic 'linear GT' (an algebraic group or torsor over Z describing linearized GT-type solutions) could be compared with the image of GT and of Gal(Q̄/Q) in GL2 and with motivic and elliptic GT. Such a scheme does not appear to be explicitly studied, but its content is modest.

missed.claim: The linearized loop equation is shown to be equivalent to an adelic equality of the Gaussian and Eisenstein norm forms. This makes visible how the elliptic points of orders 2 and 3 impose the congruences mod 4 and mod 3 on μ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a neat explicit description of the congruence-level shadow of GT. It is likely known implicitly to specialists, but this presentation does not appear in the literature.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary but tidy explicit computation of the linear (SL2(Ẑ)) shadow of the loop equation. The proposition is routine; the only forward-looking element is the brief, unproved remark about a smooth solution scheme over general rings, which is not developed.
transcription_corrections: The formula 'α0ρ(α0)^{-1} = ε2ℓ0^γ(fσ_∞f)^{-1})' is likely a garbled rendering of the commutator relation; the intended reading is [α0,ρ] = ε2ℓ0^γ[f,σ_∞].
The parameter written γ may be ν in the manuscript ('−ν' in the sign-change triple); either way γ = (μ−1)/2.
(86) reads ε3(c²+cd+u²) in the manuscript itself; this is Grothendieck's slip for d².
'trop particulier [?] manifestement' should read 'trop particulier manifestement'.
'{±1}×{±1}×Ẑ*' is as written by Grothendieck, but the third component should be μ ∈ Ẑ*, not γ.
